destinations.name: Mysuru Palace (Amba Vilas)
destinations.description: One of the most visited monuments on earth, this three-storied Indo-Saracenic royal residence of the Wodeyars features gray granite towers with deep pink marble domes, the majestic Durbar Hall with peacock-mosaic glass ceilings, the solid gold 750-kg Golden Howdah, and illumination by 97,000 electric bulbs on Sundays and during world-famous Mysuru Dasara.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Designed by British royal architect Henry Irwin and completed in 1912 after the old wooden palace burned down in 1897. Seat of the 600-year Wodeyar royal dynasty.
destinations.culturalImportance: The spiritual and royal focal point of Karnataka's state festival (Nada Habba) Mysuru Dasara.
destinations.nearestBusStation: Mysuru City Bus Stand (1 km) / Suburban Bus Stand (2 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Broad 4-lane city avenues with large tourist bus and car parking
destinations.safetyInstructions: Footwear must be deposited at designated counters outside the palace entrance. Photography prohibited in select inner royal chambers.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Mysuru Palace Board ticket required at entry gates

destinations.name: Somanathapura Keshava Temple (UNESCO)
destinations.description: A pristine 1268 CE Hoysala trikuta masterpiece dedicated to Lord Keshava, Janardhana, and Venugopala. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023, it stands on a raised 16-pointed star-shaped plinth covered from base to vimana with friezes of charging elephants, cavalry, swans, and epics carved by master sculptor Mallitamma.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Commissioned in 1268 CE by Soma Dandanayaka, a high general under Hoysala King Narasimha III.
destinations.culturalImportance: The most intact and complete Hoysala temple in existence, showing the total decorative perfection of the style.

photos.caption: Somanathapura Keshava Temple (UNESCO)
photos.source: Archaeological Survey of India & UNESCO World Heritage Centre

destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: 35 km east of Mysuru, 10 km from T. Narasipura
destinations.nearestBusStation: Somanathapura Bus Stop (0.2 km) / T. Narasipura Bus Stand (10 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Paved 2-lane scenic road running along Cauvery river countryside
destinations.safetyInstructions: Remove footwear before stepping onto the carved stone plinth. Photography without flash permitted.
destinations.permissionRequirements: ASI entry ticket required (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Archaeological Survey of India & UNESCO World Heritage Centre

destinations.name: Chamundi Hills & Monolithic Nandi
destinations.description: A 1,060-meter sacred hill overlooking Mysuru city, crowned by the 12th-century Sri Chamundeshwari Temple (one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas). En route on the historic 1,008-step stone pilgrim path rests the majestic 16-foot monolithic Nandi bull carved from single black granite in 1659 CE.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Goddess Chamundeshwari is the tutelary deity (Kula Devate) of the Maharajas of Mysuru, who vanquished demon Mahishasura on this summit.
destinations.culturalImportance: Sacred guardian peak of Mysuru; the goddess idol is carried on the 750-kg Golden Howdah atop the royal elephant during Vijayadashami.

photos.caption: Chamundi Hills & Monolithic Nandi
photos.source: Sri Chamundeshwari Temple Trust & Karnataka Tourism

destinations.nearestBusStation: Chamundi Hill Top Bus Stand (0.2 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Well-maintained ghat road with frequent city buses from Mysuru bus stand
destinations.trekkingDifficulty: Moderate (1,008 heritage stone steps from base) or Easy (by vehicle)
destinations.safetyInstructions: Traditional dress code required for temple entry. Viewpoints offer sweeping panorama of Mysuru city and palace.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Temple entry free; special darshan queue tickets optional
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Sri Chamundeshwari Temple Trust & Karnataka Tourism
